tip: The verbs звонить (zvanit) and позвонить (pazvanit = to call) take the dative person: позвоню тебе (pazvanyu tebe = I will call you).
Imperfective past marks a repeated habit: встречались каждый день (vstrechalis kazhdyy den = used to meet every day).
жаловаться на (zhalavatsya na = to complain about) takes the accusative: жалуется на головную боль (zhaluetsya na galavnuyu bol = complains about a headache).
с (s = with) takes the instrumental: соглашаемся с планом (saglashaemsya s planam = agree with the plan), from план (plan).
In the third person свой (svoy = one's own) keeps it clear: построили свой дом (pastroili svoy dom = built their own house).
вокруг (vakrug = around) takes the genitive: вокруг озера (vakrug ozera = around the lake), from озеро (ozera = lake).
Russian drops is in the present: в деревне свежий воздух (v derevne svezhiy vozdukh = in the village there is fresh air) has no verb.
Add -ее for the comparative: умнее (umneye = smarter) from умный (umnyy = smart), then чем (chem = than) for the comparison.
в plus the accusative shows motion into: светит в глаза (svetit v glaza = shines into the eyes), direction not location.
A they-verb with no subject reads as passive: продают фрукты (pradayut frukty = fruits are sold), literally they sell.
по plus the dative plural marks a recurring time: по утрам (pa utram = in the mornings), from утро (utra = morning).
Perfective verbs make the future in one word, no будем (budem) needed: купим (kupim) already means we will buy.
For weather and existence, будет (budet) alone means there will be: будет дождь (budet dozhd = there will be rain).
The verb помогать (pamagat = to help) takes the dative, so mom becomes маме (mame), not маму (mamu).
Most masculine past verbs end in the -l sound, but помог (pamog = he helped) drops it entirely.
The past ending reveals the speaker's gender: написала (napisala) ending in -la means a woman is speaking.
The verb найти (nayti = to find) has an irregular past: нашёл (nashyol = found), where the stem changes completely.
The verb быть (byt = to be) builds the future: буду (budu = I will) plus an imperfective infinitive like ждать (zhdat = to wait).
In the morning is just the instrumental used as a time word: утром (utram), from утро (utra = morning).
The word с (s = with) takes the instrumental case, turning we into с нами (s nami = with us).
For a repeated past action use the imperfective: покупал (pakupal = kept buying) fits каждый день (kazhdyy den = every day).
нужно (nuzhna = need) puts the person in the dative: ей нужно (yey nuzhna = she needs), literally to her it is needed.
A container plus its contents puts the contents in the genitive: воды (vady = of water), from вода (vada = water).
The imperfective past also means used to: открывал (atkryval = used to open) matches the habit каждое утро (kazhdaye utra = every morning).
интереснее (interesneye = more interesting) is the comparative, and чем (chem = than) introduces what it is compared against.
A few masculine nouns take a stressed -u in the location form: в саду (v sadu = in the garden), not в саде (v sade).
The word перед (pered = before) takes the instrumental: перед завтраком (pered zavtrakam = before breakfast).
By bus is на (na) plus the prepositional case: на автобусе (na avtobuse), the standard way to name transport.
писать (pisat = to write) shifts to пишет (pishet = writes) in the present, with the s sound becoming sh.
читал (chital = was reading) marks the activity with no result, while perfective дочитал (dachital = finished reading) marks completion.
